result.builder:
Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js accept several files, and open one pull request that closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104.

Right now packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js reads only process.argv[2] with readFileSync, prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` for each problem returned by lint(text) from packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js (newlines in the error become spaces), and exits 0, 1 or 2. Tests are in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (they spawn the bin with spawnSync) and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js. The docs are in packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.

Steps:
1. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js so it takes `<file> [<file> ...]`:
   - With no arguments, print a usage line (for example `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`) to stderr and exit 2.
   - If `-` appears more than once, it is a usage error: print a message to stderr and exit 2. Do this check before reading anything.
   - Go through the files in the order given. For `-`, read stdin (for example readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and use `-` as the name in the output. For any other argument, read the file, and use the argument exactly as typed in the output.
   - If a file can't be read, print `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember that it happened, and carry on with the remaining files. Do not exit early.
   - For each file, print `<file>:<line>: <error>` to stdout for each bad row, in the same format as before, keeping the newline-to-space replacement.
   - Exit code: 2 if any file couldn't be read. Otherwise 1 if any row in any file was bad. Otherwise 0.
2. Do not change packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js. lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte the same (`git diff` of that file must be empty).
3. Add node:test tests to packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, using the existing `run` helper. For stdin, call spawnSync with the `input` option. Cover these cases:
   - (a) two clean files: exit 0, no stdout;
   - (b) one bad file among several: exit 1, and only the bad file's rows are printed, with the right `<file>:<line>:` prefixes in argument order;
   - (c) `-` with clean stdin: exit 0;
   - (d) `-` with bad stdin: exit 1, output lines start with `-:`;
   - (e) a missing file among good ones: exit 2, a message on stderr, and a bad row in a later file is still reported on stdout;
   - (f) two `-` arguments: exit 2;
   - (g) no arguments: exit 2 with a usage message on stderr.
   Keep the existing tests passing.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md. Usage becomes `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`. Document that `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`, that only one `-` is allowed, that files are checked in order, and the exit codes: 0 all clean; 1 any bad row; 2 no file, a second `-`, or any file unreadable, with other files still checked and reported.
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make sure it passes.
6. Commit, push, and open one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test. The PR body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to finish on the PR head and make sure it is green. If it fails, fix the cause and push again.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head, run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) at the repository root, and then run these checks in order. Each check is PASS or FAIL. Make temporary files in a scratch directory outside the repo. In the commands below, BIN is packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js.

Check 1. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before".
Make a.jsonl = `{"a":1}\n{bad}\n`, b.jsonl = `{"b":2}\n`, c.jsonl = `{x}\n{"c":3}\n{y\n`. Run `node BIN a.jsonl b.jsonl c.jsonl` and also `node BIN c.jsonl a.jsonl`.
PASS: stdout has one line per bad row, each in the form `<file>:<line>: <error>`, using the file name exactly as given. That means a.jsonl:2, then c.jsonl:1 and c.jsonl:3 in the first run. In the second run the c.jsonl lines come before the a.jsonl line. For a single file, `node BIN a.jsonl` still prints `a.jsonl:2: <error>` as before.
FAIL: a file is skipped, the order doesn't follow the argument order, a bad row is missing, or the line format is different.

Check 2. Expect line: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)".
Run `printf '{bad}\n' | node BIN -` and `printf '{bad}\n' | node BIN b.jsonl -`. Then run `printf '{}\n' | node BIN - -`, and note its exit status.
PASS: the stdin rows are checked and reported with `-:1: ...`, and the `- -` run exits 2.
FAIL: stdin isn't read, it is reported under another name, or `- -` exits with anything other than 2.

Check 3. Expect line: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)".
Run and note exit statuses for: `node BIN b.jsonl b.jsonl` (expect 0), `node BIN b.jsonl a.jsonl` (expect 1), `node BIN` (expect 2), and `node BIN b.jsonl missing.jsonl a.jsonl` (expect 2).
PASS: every status matches. The no-argument run and the missing-file run write something to stderr. The missing-file run still prints `a.jsonl:2: ...` on stdout.
FAIL: any status is different, stderr is empty in those two runs, or the files after the missing one aren't checked and reported.

Check 4. Expect line: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged".
Run `git diff <merge-base with main>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`.
PASS: the lint function is unchanged. FAIL: the lint function's code or behaviour is changed.

Check 5. Expect line: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage".
Run `npm test` in packages/jsonl-lint and read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/test/. Then read packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
PASS: there are node:test tests for each of the seven listed cases (two clean files; one bad among several; stdin via - clean; stdin via - bad; a missing file among good ones; two - arguments; no arguments), and they pass. The README documents the multi-file usage, including `-`.
FAIL: any case has no test, the tests fail, or the README doesn't document the new usage.

Check 6. Expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
Run `gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state` and `gh pr checks <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`. Then run `npm test` at the repo root on the head.
PASS: there is one PR, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, `npm test` passes locally, and the `test` workflow run for the head commit succeeded.
FAIL: the line is missing from the body, the changes are split across more than one PR, `npm test` fails, or the workflow is failing or missing at the head.

Advisory (not pass/fail): it is nice if the second `-` is rejected before any input is read, if the usage message mentions `<file> [<file> ...]`, and if the unreadable-file message follows `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: ...`.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them; they can't be changed now. I made no code changes, commits or comments.

**Builder brief:**
- **The CLI:** rewrite `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` to take `<file> [<file> ...]` and check the files in the order given, printing `<file>:<line>: <error>` as before. A `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`.
- **Usage errors:** no arguments, or `-` given twice, exits 2. The `- -` check happens before anything is read.
- **Unreadable files:** a file that can't be read gets a message on stderr, the remaining files are still checked and reported, and the run exits 2. Otherwise it exits 1 if any row in any file is bad, and 0 if all files are clean.
- **Other files:** `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` stays untouched. New tests go in `packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js`, one per listed case. The README gets the new usage and exit codes.
- **The PR:** run `npm test`, then open one PR whose body says `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, and make sure the `test` workflow passes on its latest commit.

**Verifier brief:** six checks, one per expect line, in the issue's order. Each one runs something on the PR's latest commit. Checks 1–3 run the CLI on small sample files and test the output order and exit codes, including stdin, `- -` and a missing file between good ones. Check 4 diffs `src/index.js` against `main`. Check 5 runs the package's tests and reads them and the README. Check 6 checks the PR body, the workflow result and a local `npm test`.

The finer points the expect lines don't name are under an "Advisory" heading in the verifier brief, so they can't fail a PR. These are: rejecting the second `-` before reading input, the exact usage message, and the exact wording of the unreadable-file message.
